reading.body:
CyrusOne's Florence, Kentucky campus is the state's largest published data center at 5 MW of IT capacity, but it is an enterprise facility, not an AI training site.

The published figures describe a conventional colocation campus: 5 MW across 143,000 square feet of technical space, with certifications for financial services, healthcare, federal systems, and audit compliance. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, that 5 MW supports roughly 125 racks. The certification set points to regulated enterprise and cloud tenants, which is a different workload profile from the high-density GPU deployments that drive AI scaling.

Kentucky's disclosed data center capacity totals 9.55 MW across three facilities that publish figures, with five mapped facilities overall. Most mapped facilities do not publish power specifications, so the installed base is likely larger than the disclosed number. Either way, Kentucky is a small node in the national footprint and does not register as a center of AI scaling by published capacity.

What the data does not cover is decisive here. It says nothing about the local grid, about whether CyrusOne or an acquirer will retrofit this campus for higher-density workloads, or about any announced expansion. The suitability score of 50 reflects only published IT capacity and operator type, and lists announced expansion as missing. Whether this facility matters to AI depends on facts the specifications do not contain.
